matt: @here Seeing huge queue growth on hosted-api-us-east. p95 -> 3s, p99 -> 22s, several client timeouts. Request backlog up from ~120 to ~6.2k in 10m. 503s starting to show. :rotating_light:

sre_oncall_amber: Paging in. Amber oncall here, joining. Matt can you paste the top logs and which model pools are impacted?

matt: Topline: GPU pool 'hosted-gpu-shared' saturated, autoscaler attempted provisioning but VM creation errors and API quota errors. quick logs: ```autoscaler: failed to create instance: QuotaExceeded: Insufficient GPU quota; request 8xA10 -> denied
provisioner: rate-limited, retry-after=30s
provisioner: pending-creations=250
```

incident-bot: PagerDuty alert PD12345 triggered (severity: high) for hosted-api-us-east. On-call: @sre_oncall_amber.

leah: I see a secondary issue: the cluster cloud quota is fine for cores but GPUs are hitting a soft quota. We recently bumped some partner pools. Might be allocation leak.

eng-runtime-ryan: Confirmed. Autoscaler logs show repeated CreateInstance(…) -> 403 QuotaExceeded and occasional 429 from cloud-provisioner. Also a recent deploy (today 09:05) increased default batch-size which spiked token churn. Pushing rollback now?

matt: Traffic pattern shows an external customer partner sent a sudden job-batch fanout. It's a small subset but extremely bursty.

sre_oncall_amber: Triage/mitigation plan: 1) Short-term: apply emergency global rate limit on hosted-api to reduce new requests and let queue drain. 2) Route high-cost model calls to cpu-backed fallback if acceptable. 3) Try to spin up dedicated burst pool in another region (us-west) and failover. 4) Open ticket with cloud quota and escalate.

leah: I'm applying a temporary global ingress throttle: setting header-rate-limit to 90rps across hosted-api routes (was unrestricted). Doing now.

ops-bot: Command accepted: set-rate-limit --scope=hosted-api --limit=90rps --reason="emergency-gpu-exhaustion"

matt: Throttle applied. New requests visibly dropped, queue growth rate slowed but backlog still high (~4.7k). p99 down to 10s.

eng-runtime-ryan: Implementing fallback routing rule: if model in request in high-cost list -> route to quantized-variant (gptx-q4). Will add header X-Fallback: true. Patch pushed to routing service. ```PATCH /routing/rules { "if": "model in high_cost", "route": "gptx-q4" }```

incident-bot: Automation: applied routing fallback for 2min window to test.

customer-success-dave: Heads up — I'm seeing customers report timeouts to support queue. I flagged the top 3 accounts with SRE priority: Acme Corp (enterprise), BrightHealth (partner), InlineAI. Acme is on a paid SLA. We should update status page.

sre_oncall_amber: Agree. Matt can you draft a short status update? I'll mark SEV2 for tracking.

matt: Status update posted to status.redwood.ai: "Investigating increased error rates and latencies in hosted-api-us-east due to GPU provisioning failures. Mitigations in progress: rate limiting, fallback routing. Some customers may see degraded latency or 503s." Link: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/5523456789

infra: I've opened a priority support ticket with cloud provider (case #CL-987654). Raised for quota override and provisioning throttles. They replied with ETA 45-60m.

eng-runtime-ryan: We're also enabling a hot-route to the Dedicated short-burst pool (dedicated-burst-2) in us-west and mass-migrating queued requests that can tolerate cross-region latency. Doing a canary 50 requests first.

matt: Canary looks okay, success for 45/50. Starting broader failover TTL=5m.

leah: Queue reduced to 1.3k, p99 ~3.5s. Good progress. Leaving rate limit in place for now.

sre_oncall_amber: Next steps: - keep rate limit - keep fallback routing - leave failover running until cloud quota update or queue <200 - prepare postmortem. Also note we rolled back the batch-size deploy (ryan took that action).

eng-runtime-ryan: Rolled back default batch-size to previous 1.2x. That's stopped the token-churn spike. Commit: `revert batch-size deploy 2026-03-15T09:05`

customer-success-dave: I updated the 3 impacted customers and offered temporary credits. Acme Ops wants a direct contact. I'll escalate to sales engineering.

ops-bot: Incident declared: incident-5523456789 (sev=2). Channel #incidents linked.

matt: We're at backlog ~340, p99 ~1.2s. Autoscaler still showing some pending creates but provider ETA 45m.

sre_oncall_amber: Good. I'll keep monitoring for 30m then hand off to night oncall @harry-night-oncall. Amber out. :thumbsup:

harry-night-oncall: Acknowledge and joining for handoff. Quick confirm: outstanding actions?

sre_oncall_amber: Handoff summary for @harry-night-oncall: 1) Rate limit active (90rps). 2) Fallback routing to gptx-q4 enabled. 3) Failover to dedicated-burst-2 in us-west active for cross-region tolerant requests. 4) Cloud provider ticket CL-987654 open (ETA 45-60m). 5) Queue decreasing, target <200 to resolve. 6) Postmortem placeholder created. Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INC/5523456789

harry-night-oncall: Thanks. I'll stand watch and escalate if backlog growth resumes. If cloud ETA misses, next action is to expand cross-region failover and consider short-term premium instance purchase.

sre_oncall_amber: Leaving docs and timeline in the incident playbook. All teams clear for now.

incident-bot: Incident update logged: mitigations applied: rate-limit, rollback, fallback routing, cross-region failover.

matt: Adding final note: root cause appears to be a combination of client-driven fanout + an inadvertent batch-size change + cloud provider hard quota enforcement. We'll capture the RCA after postmortem.

customer-success-dave: Customers notified and actioned. No revenue-impacting SLA breach at this time (Acme reported degraded performance but not a hard outage).

harry-night-oncall: Taking ownership. Will post an update at +1h. Signing off from active watch for now.
